subject: Urban Planning
title: Open Defecation: A Global Crisis
description: A quick win: understand Open Defecation: A Global Crisis.

hook.text: 494 million people worldwide practice open defecation. That's one in every 15 humans with no toilet access.

buildup.text: In rural India, millions of homes lack toilets. Cultural stigma and water scarcity make building latrines difficult.

discovery.text: India's Swachh Bharat mission built 110 million toilets between 2014 and 2019 — the largest sanitation project in history.

twist.text: Building toilets isn't enough. Many new toilets go unused because of cultural practices and lack of running water.

climax.text: Sanitation prevents 1.5 million child deaths annually from diarrheal diseases. A toilet is a life-saving device.

punchline.text: The toilet is humanity's greatest health invention. Half a billion people lack one.

quiz.question: What was the Swachh Bharat mission?
options: A UN program providing clean water to African nations
India's campaign that built 110 million toilets in five years
A global initiative to end plastic pollution in rivers
